the behaviours teachers used in their lessons were generally associated with pupils' positive rather than negative psychosocial growth and that the quality of instruction teachers provided in urban schools in the United Kingdom was similar to that of teachers in rural areas.
the teachers in this study used behaviours positively associated with pupils' development much more frequently and behaviours negatively associated with pupils much less frequently.

the behaviours teachers use in their teaching of physical education in the United Kingdom, as assessed by the Coaching Behavior Assessment system, are similar across urban and rural settings and that, overall, teachers use more behaviours positively associated with pupils' development than those negatively associated with it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the National Curriculum for physical education has influenced the behaviours of teachers working in urban schools.
the quality of teaching provided by teachers in a depressed urban environment and the extent to which their behaviours are influenced by the National Curriculum for physical education.
the influence of the National Curriculum on the quality of instruction that teachers provide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the National Curriculum for physical education has been successful in promoting the use of positive teaching behaviours in urban secondary schools.
, in the urban context, teachers' behaviours were associated with pupils' positive rather than negative psychosocial outcomes.

teachers working in inner-city schools are more likely than those in rural settings to use behaviours that are positively linked with pupils' psychocultural development and that are negatively linked with pupils' negative psychological development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the National Curriculum for physical education has had a positive effect on teachers' behaviour in terms of their use of behaviours positively associated with pupils' psychological development.
the behaviours used by teachers in this study were generally associated with pupils' positive development.
, in general terms, British teachers' use of behaviours positively and negatively linked with pupils' psychocial development was similar across the urban and rural settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that

teachers working in a range of settings can be encouraged and supported in the use of behaviours that promote pupils' positive psychomotor and psychosocial development and in the avoidance of those that promote negative psychomotor and/or psychosocial development.
the National Curriculum does not appear to have had a detrimental impact on teachers' behaviours related to pupils psychosocial development, at least in urban settings.
teachers working with pupils in Years 8, 9, and 10, in the United Kingdom, are providing a positive psychosocial environment in which pupils can learn.
